thesis: The speaker argues that despite the immense talent and hard work of Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger, Berkshire Hathaway only made about one good investment every five years, suggesting that finding such opportunities is inherently difficult. He posits that this scarcity exists because investors must stay within their circle of competence, which expands slowly over time, and cites the Sea & Candy investment as a 'stretch' that taught the founders about brands and pricing power, a lesson that was essential for their later confidence in making the massive Coca-Cola bet.
